static func policy(for provider: ProviderKind, _ launch: HydraLaunch) -> String {
        let maxHeads = launch.maxHeads
        let autoMerges = launch.autoMerges
        let reviewsHeads = launch.reviewsHeads
        let projects = launch.projects
        // The pair's routable profiles, in the words the lead routes with: on Claude and
        // Copilot the profile's agent variant, on Codex the model and effort to pass.
        let profiles = nativeRoutableProfiles(of: launch)
        let profileRule: String
        if profiles.isEmpty {
            profileRule = ""
        } else {
            switch provider {
            case .claude, .copilot:
                let variants = profiles.map { "`\(workerAgentName(for: $0))` for \($0.name)" }.joined(separator: ", ")
                profileRule = " Some heads are tuned for a purpose: route the task to \(variants) instead of the plain `\(workerAgentName)` when the work belongs to that purpose."
            case .codex:
                let routes = profiles.map { profile -> String in
                    var parts: [String] = []
                    if let model = profile.model { parts.append("`model` = \(model)") }
                    if let effort = profile.effort { parts.append("`reasoning_effort` = \(effort)") }
                    return "\(profile.name) (pass \(parts.joined(separator: " and ")))"
                }.joined(separator: ", ")
                profileRule = " Some heads are tuned for a purpose: route the task by passing the profile's own knobs in `spawn_agent` — \(routes) — when the work belongs to that purpose."
            default:
                profileRule = ""
            }
        }
        let howToSpawn: String
        let howToWait: String
        switch provider {
        case .claude:

Native heads are bounded by the provider, via the prompt sentence for Claude/Copilot and agents.max_concurrent_threads_per_session for Codex, which is OMITTED entirely when maxHeads is nil (Hydra.swift:830-831).

DroppyCode/App/AppModel+HydraMerge.swift:158-174 isScratchPath. Roots, in order: Storage.worktreesDirectory.path, NSTemporaryDirectory(), "/tmp", "/private/tmp", "/var/folders", "/private/var/folders", then <home>/Library. Separately, any path directly under home whose first component starts with "." is scratch (:163-164). The /private double-spelling trick is :165-168 and exists because standardizingPath only drops a leading /private while the file still exists. hydraProject (DroppyCode/App/AppModel+Hydra.swift:278-300) requires expanded.hasPrefix("/") before the repository walk (:288) and terminates the upward walk at "/" (:296), with an explicit dir.isEmpty -> "/" guard (:298).
cross_cutting_verified.port_impact_windows: Windows needs a re-expressed root set (%TEMP%, %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp, the app's worktrees folder, %APPDATA%/%LOCALAPPDATA% in place of ~/Library) and a dotted-folder-under-profile rule. The absolute-path test must accept a drive-letter root and a UNC root instead of a leading '/', and the upward walk must terminate at the drive or share root. This is an ENGINEERING DECISION the port must make explicitly; the source offers no Windows form.

cross_cutting_verified.claim: Worktree copy folder naming is '<longest project slug>-<persona slug>[-<round>]-<8 lowercase hex of thread UUID>'.
cross_cutting_verified.truth: WRITER (DroppyCode/App/AppModel+Hydra.swift:492-495): folder = project.name with SPACES replaced by "-" then lowercased — nothing else is replaced, so dots, underscores and slashes survive. name = info.persona.name with spaces replaced by "-" then lowercased, so "Tova 2" becomes "tova-2" and the round is not a separate field. suffix = String(head.id.uuidString.lowercased().prefix(8)) — the first 8 characters of the UUID string, which are hex. path = Storage.worktreesDirectory / "<folder>-<name>-<suffix>". The writer uses the head's OWN project name, never a "longest" anything. SWEEPER (DroppyCode/App/AppModel+Hydra.swift:1029-1051): it is the sweeper that picks the LONGEST project slug that prefixes the folder name (:1038), then splits the remainder on "-", requires >= 2 parts, pops the last and requires it to be exactly 8 characters and all hex digits (:1041), drops a trailing all-digit round part when exactly 2 parts remain (:1042), requires the single remaining part to be a known persona slug (:1043), and skips folders younger than 600 seconds (:1044). A folder a live thread names is never touched (:1032, :1035). Removal is git worktree remove first, FileManager.removeItem as fallback (:1047-1049).
cross_cutting_verified.port_impact: Keep both halves consistent: the writer's space-only slug and the sweeper's longest-prefix match, 8-hex suffix, optional numeric round, persona-set membership, and the 600 s grace period. On Windows a project name may contain characters that are legal in the name but illegal in a path; the source's slug does not sanitize them, and a port that adds sanitizing must add the same sanitizing to the sweeper or the sweep stops matching.

cross_cutting_verified.claim: The fence dialects diverge on purpose: delegationOpener accepts hydra, hydra-sent and hydra-leaving; the streaming readers accept only hydra and hydra-sent.

cross_cutting_verified.claim: Native-provider wiring is three different shapes from one HydraLaunch.
cross_cutting_verified.truth: Claude (Hydra.swift:741-774): an object keyed by agent name; each agent object carries description, prompt, background(false), and for the SCOUT ONLY tools ["Read","Grep","Glob","WebFetch","WebSearch"]; model added only when workerModel != nil && != "default"; effort added only when workerEffort is non-empty. Profile variants clone the WORKER (so no tools) with a rewritten description and the profile's own model/effort. Copilot (Hydra.swift:776-825): an ARRAY of objects with name, displayName, description, prompt, infer(true); model only when != "auto"; reasoningEffort when non-empty; tools NEVER emitted for any Copilot agent. Codex (Hydra.swift:827-840): ["agents": {max_concurrent_threads_per_session when maxHeads != nil, default_subagent_model when workerModel non-empty, default_subagent_reasoning_effort when workerEffort non-empty}, "features": {multi_agent: true always, multi_agent_v2: {expose_spawn_agent_model_overrides: true} only when nativeRoutableProfiles is non-empty}]. Note 'agents' is emitted even when empty. The critique's list is right except that it omits Claude's scout tools array while listing 'tools' as a Claude key.

cross_cutting_verified.claim: GitLab merge requests bypass the shared forge layer with a specific glab argument vector and two retries.
cross_cutting_verified.truth: DroppyCode/App/AppModel+HydraMerge.swift:329-399. Gate (:330): only when await git.forge() == .gitlab AND LoginEnvironment.which("glab") != nil; otherwise git.createPullRequest. Vector, in order: ["mr","create","--title",title,"--description",body,"--yes"], then ["--repo", <remoteWebURL with user and password stripped via URLComponents>] only when remoteWebURL() has a host, then ["--source-branch",source,"--target-branch",target]. Pre-check (:350-352): hydraGitLabAuthFailure runs ["auth","status"] with timeout 30 in git.directory; a THROW from Shell.run is treated as "no failure" (nil) and a non-zero exit is a failure whose message, or the literal "glab is not signed in to this GitLab host." when empty, is thrown as HydraMergeRequestError.gitLabAuth(host:branch:detail:). Main run (:354) timeout 300. Retry 1 (:356-366): only when isGitLabAuthFailure AND a fresh auth status now passes; same vector, timeout 300. Retry 2 (:370-374): when mentionsRecoverFile, the vector PLUS "--recover" appended at the end, timeout 300. isGitLabAuthFailure (:390-394) lowercases output + "\n" + errorOutput and matches "401" OR "unauthorized" OR ("authentication" AND ("failed" OR "expired" OR "invalid" OR "required")). mentionsRecoverFile (:397-399) is a lowercased "recover" substring test. Squash and remove-source-branch are deliberately not passed.
cross_cutting_verified.port_impact: Reproduce the vector order, the two timeouts (30 s and 300 s), the throw-means-nil quirk in the auth pre-check, both retry predicates, and the substring heuristics verbatim including the four authentication co-words.

cross_cutting_verified.claim: The auto-merge never checks out a branch.
cross_cutting_verified.truth: DroppyCode/App/AppModel+HydraMerge.swift:211-255. head = git.commitHash(); tree = git.captureTree(paths: sorted); if tree == git.treeHash(of: "HEAD") the merge returns .alreadyOnMain and says nothing. patch = git.diff(from: head, to: tree); files parsed off the main actor. ownBranch = current == nil || current == target, where current = git.status()?.branch and target = git.defaultBranch(); branch = ownBranch ? hydraBranchName(for: lead) : current!. commit = git.commitWork(tree, parent: head, message:). commitHash() is READ AGAIN (:241) and a mismatch aborts with "Hydra did not merge: the checkout moved while it worked." Then git.updateRef("refs/heads/<branch>", to: commit, expecting: ownBranch ? nil : head) (:248) — expecting nil means the ref must not exist. Only when !ownBranch does git.resetIndex(paths: sorted) run (:252). No checkout, no git commit, no stash anywhere in the path.

upstream_defects.title: The lead's whole closing instruction block can be rendered inside the last head's report card.
upstream_defects.what_happens: reportMessage joins its closing array into one paragraph. withoutLeadInstructions drops that paragraph only when it starts with one of nine prefixes. When no head landed cleanly, the paragraph can start with '<A> and <B> both changed <path>: ...' (Hydra.swift:1267) or "<Name>'s changes would not apply on their own; ..." (Hydra.swift:1271), neither of which is a prefix, so the block including 'Do not check any of this...' and the report style rule is shown to the user as if the head had written it.

upstream_defects.title: mergeStatus's .failed branch silently drops the pending-files sentence.
upstream_defects.what_happens: The .merged and .stray branches both append `pending`; the .failed branch does not. After a failed merge the lead is never told how many files are still unmerged, even though the caller computed the number.

upstream_defects.title: An empty-string 'name' or 'project' in a delegation entry shadows its alias instead of falling through.
upstream_defects.what_happens: `{"name": "", "head": "Otto"}` produces an unnamed head; `{"project": "", "repo": "gaze-site"}` produces a head in the chat's own project. The ?? is over the optional, not over emptiness.

upstream_defects.title: Turning on the per-chat Hydra switch can silently change the chat's model and effort.
upstream_defects.what_happens: 'Turn Hydra on for this chat' adopts the remembered pair's orchestratorModel and orchestratorEffort. Nothing in the menu says so and there is no undo.

upstream_defects.title: A pair whose worker provider is unavailable silently loses its workerModel as well as falling back to the lead's provider.
upstream_defects.what_happens: The user-facing note says only that the heads run on the lead's provider for now; it does not say the pair's chosen head model was dropped and the lead's own model used instead.

upstream_defects.title: 'Clear finished heads' leaves the heads popover open while every other action closes it.
spawnWaitingHeads ignores the concurrency ceiling when the launch is nil.
upstream_defects.what_happens: If Hydra is switched off (app-wide or per chat) between a delegation block arriving and the waiting queue being swept, hydraLaunch returns nil and every queued head is dispatched in one loop with no ceiling.

upstream_defects.title: hydraHeadsFallbackNote and hydraHeadsProvider disagree on what 'installed' means.
upstream_defects.evidence: DroppyCode/App/AppModel+Hydra.swift:117 uses providers.countsAsInstalled(provider); :126 uses providers.status(provider).isInstalled to choose the wording.
upstream_defects.what_happens: A provider that countsAsInstalled but is not isInstalled (or the reverse) can produce a note whose reason does not match why the fallback happened.

upstream_defects.title: HydraMergePopover's files-line regex accepts only U+2212, while HydraReportsPopover's accepts U+2212 or a hyphen.
upstream_defects.what_happens: Two readers of two very similar app-written lines have different tolerance. The merge card degrades to plain text on any minus variance; the report card does not.

upstream_defects.title: delegations(fromBody:) cannot distinguish 'the JSON did not parse' from 'every entry was rejected'.
upstream_defects.what_happens: A well-formed array of entries that all lack a prompt makes delegations(in:) walk back over every earlier fence and finally the whole message tail, which can accidentally parse something unrelated, before reporting the block unreadable.
